preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100000 and int(line.split()[0]) != int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) and m (1 ≤ m ≤ 100 000). Each of the next m lines contains two distinct integers x_i and y_i (1 ≤ x_i, y_i ≤ n) representing bidirectional roads between cities.
The input has exactly m + 1 lines: one for n and m, and m lines for roads.

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the minimum number of separate cities after orienting all roads unidirectionally.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The input roads are valid and connect existing cities.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == min(sum(1 for city in range(1, n + 1) if all(not (city == x and y == city) for x, y in orientations) and any((city == x and y == city) for x, y in orientations) or (not any((city == x and y == city) for x, y in orientations) and not any((city == y and x == city) for x, y in orientations))) for orientations in possible_orientations)
postconditions.description: The output is the minimum number of cities with no incoming roads (separate cities) across all possible valid orientations of the roads. A city is separate if no road leads into it (no incoming edge).
